reasons.C: Long balanced periods joined by semicolons, 'every one ... his', inserted 'I think', Latinate period diction and a firm, faintly ironic stance towards the grumblers closely match the passage's movement and tone.
reasons.A: Period register and semicolon-joined sentences fit, but stacked similes (shuttles, web, tide) and the soft 'remedy is not a revolution' hedging lay the ornament on thicker and gentler than the passage's blunter assertion.
reasons.B: Modern movement and diction ('everyone ... their', short declaratives, 'a small tax on everyone's time', few semicolons) read as a contemporary plain-style writer, not the author.
